MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD SPECIAL PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, APRIL 14, 2021

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Special Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, April 14, 2021 in the Council
Chambers on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge of
Allegiance by Commissioner Patrick, the meeting was called to order
at 7:03p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:

Present:  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide’ Trejo
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams
  Chairman Larry Springs

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner
  Arturo Salazar, Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner
  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., ECD Director
  Jeff Lewis, Assistant City Attorney
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary
  Via Community Phone Call Coverage:
  AT&T Conference Call Operator Rep.

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:

Ms. Wilcox stated that Bernard McCrumby has been promoted to Senior
Planner, staff received one item of correspondence for Item 5A, there
is a revised ordinance for Item 5B, which was posted on the City’s
website, and last staff is requesting the closing of tonight’s
special planning commission meeting in the name of Mrs. Mariah
Jeter-Hudson, the late mother of Ms. Cynthia Robinson, staff
assistant.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

None, and the AT&T Operator verbally confirmed that there were no
participants on the line to speak.

(5) PUBLIC HEARING:

5A. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2021-002(SP-2021-002) 10006 SOUTH
INGLEWOOD AVENUE: A public hearing to consider an application by
Christopher Wadleigh, representing Cotti Foods for Special Use
Permit No. 2021-002 (SP-2021-002) to allow the conversion of a former
service station site into an approximately 2,445 square-foot fast
food restaurant with a drive through on an approximately 23,144
square-foot, C-2A (Airport Commercial) zoned property at 10006 South
Inglewood Avenue

Mr. Arturo Salazar, Planner made the presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

  1
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
April 14, 2021

Commissioner Patrick asked staff questions regarding the ability for
customers entering and exiting the property, along with turning
restrictions, and Mr. Salazar answered her question.

Commissioner Rice asked staff several questions regarding the
entering and exiting of vehicles on both Inglewood Avenue and Century
Boulevard’s and questioned if it is a ticketed offense to do illegal
turning from the applicant’s parking area. Also asked about the
volume of the drive-thru parking area speakers, and if they will
disturb any of the surrounding residents.
- Mr. Salazar stated yes it can be a ticketed offense, and explained
  further regarding how the applicant will have marked areas and
  painted ground markings as to entering and exiting of the parking
  areas.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
 The location on the property where the employees will park their
  vehicles on the lot? Will it take away from customers to park their
  vehicles if they wanted to dine-in?
   Mr. Salazar stated there was plenty of parking on the lot along
  with public transit.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked staff –
 Asked about the number of security cameras on both the interior
  and exterior of this project.
   Mr. Salazar stated that the entire project at present has seven
  cameras total, but if the Commission deems it necessary for more
  security cameras on the property, it can be made a condition
  of approval for the applicant.

Chairman Springs asked staff several questions, and Mr. Salazar
answered his questions.

Chairman Springs opened the phone lines for the applicant to present
his project to the Planning Commission.

Both Mr. Christopher Wadleigh, Sr. V.P., Design and Development of
Cotti Foods and Mr. John Austin, Architect on this project, came
forward to present their project to the planning commission

Commissioner Patrick spoke to the applicants regarding the layout
of the property next door, the applicant stated they only are able
to work with their subject location and nothing outside of the project
site.

Commissioner Trejo asked several questions of the applicant
regarding the restaurant having the capability to have outside-line
busters and to have them working upon opening day. Also, that in order
to cut down on drive-thru traffic-backup, not only on opening day
of the restaurant, but also on event days at all of the entertainment
venues in the City and Mr. Wadleigh stated that it can and will be
done to insure no traffic-backup onto the streets of Inglewood Avenue
and Century Boulevard.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked the applicants regarding the hours
of operation for both the drive-thru and the sit-down area in the
restaurant, and are they both open from 7:00am until 1:00am, seven
days a week. The applicant responded with the requested information.

Chairman Springs opened up the floor for public comments to speak
for or against this project.

  2
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
April 14, 2021

FOR / AGAINST

None. This was affirmed by the AT&T On-line Operator.

MOTION:
The motion was made by Commissioner Rice to affirm categorical
exemption EA-CE-2021-015, and adopt a resolution recommending City
Council adoption of SP-2021-002 and was seconded by Commissioner
Patrick, that Resolution No. 1893;

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY PLANNING COMMISSION OF
  THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING A
  CERTAIN SPECIAL USE PERMIT FOR CHRISTOPHER
  WADLEIGH REPRESENTING COTTI FOODS TO ALLOW THE
  CONVERSION OF A VACANT FORMER SERVICE STATIONF
  SITE INTO AN APPROXIMATELY 2,445 SQUARE-FOOT
  FAST FOOD RESTAURANT WITH A DRIVE THROUGH ON AN
  APPROXIMATELY 23,144 SQUARE-FOOT C-2A (AIRPORT
  COMMERCIAL) ZONED PROPERTY LOCATED AT 10006
  SOUTH INGLEWOOD AVENUE

Be approved.

The motion passed by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Shaw-Williams and
  Chairman Springs

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeals process.

5B. ZONING CODE AMENDMENT NO. 2020-001 (ZCA-2020-001) CHAPTER 12 IMC:
A public hearing to consider Zoning Code Amendment 2020-001
(ZCA-2020-001) to Chapter 12 of the Inglewood Municipal Code to
modify regulations for off-hour parking for major event patrons and
tailgating, citywide.

Mr. Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner, made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick stated that she had no questions.

Commissioner Rice stated to staff:
 What are the ranges and boundaries of the red-line around the
  stadium and what does that red broken or hatch-marked line
  represent?
   Mr. McCrumby stated that the red line represents a complete
  One-mile boundary around the Hollywood Park area from point to
  point on the map to insure that it is a full and complete one-mile
  radius of properties that may participate in the tailgating
  process. The red broken or hatch-marked lines represent the
  City’s boundary lines.
 Is the measurement from the center point of the property where the
  one-mile radius starts?
   Mr. McCrumby stated that the one-mile radius is from the
  exterior property lines of the Hollywood Park area, and then
  the one-mile radius is determined from those points.

  3
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
April 14, 2021

  One concern is who did the determination of where the one-mile
  radius starts and stops? It seems that the entire City is included
  within this one-mile, so much so, we show the red-line passing Van
  Ness Avenue.
   Mr. McCrumby stated that per the direction staff received from
  the Planning Commission after the last PC Meeting, in order to
  insure that all businesses may have an opportunity to partake
  in the tailgating process, this was why staff went with the
  one-mile radius map.
   Ms. Wilcox stated that it was the City of Inglewood’s GIS
  Department that depicted the one-mile radius throughout the
  entire City utilizing the property line all around the Hollywood
  Park project itself.

Chairman Springs stated:
 This is what we the planning commission asked for, correct?
Commissioner Rice stated:
 Yes, I just thought that the center point would be the determining
  factor for the one-mile radius.
 With the inclusion of the entire City, several of the smaller
  parking areas throughout the City will have a very hard time in
  attempting to control large Recreational Vehicles that will have
  challenged our definition of tailgating, with them trying to
  set-up with extra-large barbeque grills and tents, lots of people
  and no control or regulation of the tailgaters, so as to not bombard
  Code Enforcement with that task. There needs to be the installation
  of Hosts who will regulate those who mainly come just for the
  tailgating alone.
 I personally feel that the Planning Commission is going to have
  to condition this one-mile radius with what one would call a
  modified tailgate or have it under very strong control with a Host
  who has a vested interest in making sure that this can be regulated,
  along with other conditions and considerations for this to work
  for this City. He stated he would like to come back later on this
  evening with more ideas for this project.

Chairman Springs called Commissioner Trejo.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff:
 With regards to the one-mile radius, for the tailgating, only the
  so-called arterial streets within a one-mile radius?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that yes, only the major arterials that are
  allowed to have the major event parking and if your lot is not
  eligible for the major event parking, you will not be able to
  host tailgating.
 Regarding the Major Event Parking, who determines that status for
  the open parking lots?
   Mr. McCrumby stated the major event parking is determined by
  staff.
 When utilizing the renewal process for tailgating permits, who
  will closely monitor the tailgating hosts, will there be an
  enforcement component in monitoring the tailgating applicants,
  what about situations that most likely will come up, such as law
  enforcement and/or the community, who is going to be the one who
  will know if the applicants are following the rules and regulations
  of the tailgating process.
   Mr. McCrumby stated that the City utilizes a division call
  Permits and Licenses, which is made up of representatives from
  a number of different divisions in City Hall, and they will
  determine the factors with regards to compliance by all
  applicants.

  4
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
April 14, 2021

   Ms. Wilcox stated that when it is time for the applicants’ yearly
  renewal, they go before an annual board hearing review, and they
  will hear from IPD , code enforcement, finance to see how the
  applicant has conducted itself, and if there were any violations
  or calls to their particular location.
  So say that there are several lots that qualify for the tailgating
  license and they have a spill-over of vehicles, will the community
  or public have a phone number to call to complain or someone in
  charge who will be making sure that the applicants are true to
  following the requirements and conditions of the ordinance
  required for the tailgating license? What about if there are
  complaints from the adjoining neighbors with regards to the noise,
  and the loud music and the loud actions of the tailgaters?
   Ms. Wilcox stated that hasn’t been included in the ordinance,
  but typically when they are renewing a license, code enforcement
  will check to see if there are any code violations that may have
  been brought against the site and police would have checked for
  any calls received associated with the site, and if there were
  any against the site, it would be noted at the applicant’s
  renewal hearing with P&L.
  Only the major arterial streets that are noted here, if they
  qualify for major events parking, will be the only ones who will
  be able to host tailgating, correct?
   Mr. McCrumby stated that is correct.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams stated:
 Her concern is if there are several complaints prior to the annual
  renewal process, can the license be pulled prior to the annual
  review date?
   Mr. McCrumby stated yes, it can be pulled. As the planning
  division is a part of the permits and licensing body of
  departments, we will create a list of standards for every
  applicant that applies for the tailgating license issued. It
  will state that if the conditions are not met, their license
  will be revoked, there will be language that P&L will regulate
  and monitor all of the permits given.

Chairman Springs asked Mr. McCrumby;
 For clarification on the location of the tailgating areas which
  are supposed to be within one mile of Hollywood Park on a
  non-residential, commercial approved lot. There is a property that
  has a vacant lot and is located on 12th Avenue and Pincay, so would
  that location be allowed to have tailgating there?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated no, not at that location, because it does
  not follow the conditions and guidelines of the ordinance for
  tailgating, non-residential, commercial approved, one mile
  away from the stadium, licensed lot. Therefore if those
  conditions are not met, no tailgating permits and license will
  be given.

Chairman Springs stated to the Planning Commission that for final
questions to staff, they will only be allowed 3 minutes and to have
staff set the timer per planning commissioner and their question for
staff.

Commissioner Patrick stated she had no questions.

Commissioner Rice asked Commissioner Patrick if he may obtain her
3 minutes and add them to his 3 minutes, Commissioner Patrick approved
Commissioner Rice’s request.

  5
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
April 14, 2021

Commissioner Rice asked staff;
 He wants to clarify with planning staff regarding the statement
  that says this regulation is based on data specific to Inglewood,
  what does that mean?
   Mr. McCrumby stated that staff went up to Northern California,
  as far East as Massachusetts and South, to see how they conduct
  and allow tailgating and how it takes place on several of the
  stadium parking lots there – majority of the tailgating happens
  at those various stadium locations only. Based on this research,
  Inglewood is distinguishing itself from most other cities with
  the one-mile radius around the stadium in allowing some of the
  business owners in the area to benefit from the tailgating
  activity.
 Here is an opportunity for the City as a whole to be able to benefit
  from this new venture, not only for the stadium, but also for the
  business owners here in the City along the arterial corridor. We
  cannot let this pass the City by, and in doing so, we need to have
  what is called Modified Tailgating, by making sure that each
  location has a Host for the tailgating and a food truck assigned
  to that location, so much so they will take care and take control
  of the music, take care of the clean-up of the left-over food,
  plates, cups and merchandise even after the tailgating is over and
  insure that there will be no competition of music and multiple
  grills and cooks attempting to outdo one another. With the Host
  conducting the modified tailgating, whether there are 10/20/30
  cars on the lot, the hosts will make sure that the property owner
  will not lose its license for the tailgating because of the
  potential monies they can acquire.
 As the Hosts, they will need to have multiple trucks, one with
  stadium merchandise and the other with food and drinks – with all
  items for sale, which will generate a lot of revenue for everyone,
  the property owner, the stadium, and the City.
 What it is for the City is we are offering to fit a square peg
  (because our tailgating situation looks nothing like what is going
  on across the country) into a round hole and make sure that it works
  for everyone involved. Here in Inglewood everything that we do here
  is unique, we have to do our own thing. Although we can look at
  other cities and states and see how they run things for them, but
  I truly believe that the business owners here in Inglewood can run
  their own properties, host their own events and take care of
  business and patrons where everyone will benefit.

Chairman Springs stated that Commissioner’s Rice time has expired,
and stated to staff;
 That at the time of making a motion, most likely Commissioner Rice
  can add and make some additional conditions that can be then
  handled by staff prior to delivery to the City Council, is that
  correct?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that is correct.

Commissioner Trejo stated to staff;
 I understand what Commissioner Rice is stating, and feels that the
  property owners will need to be protected from the individuals that
  will try to come into Inglewood, who may have more than 2 or 3 beers
  and lose all inhibitions and try to take over the area with their
  own loud music, lots of trash making with their left overs, and
  to stop this from happening to the property owner losing his
  license to have the tailgating, it could be in the form of each
  property owner having a host, with the special food truck to ensure
  that the property owner gets to keep their license. I don’t know
  how we can condition this in the ordinance, but it will help to
  protect the property owners and the City as well.

  6
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
April 14, 2021

Chairman Springs called on Commissioner Shaw-Williams and she
stated;
 She also is in agreement with Commissioner Rice that the property
  owners will need to have a host and to opt for a Modified Tailgating
  event.

Chairman Springs opened the public hearing and the phone lines from
the AT&T operator to hear from the public to say “For or Against”
this item.
FOR / AGAINST:
None (Confirmed by the AT&T Operator)
Commissioner Rice asked to make a statement:
 I think that there will need to be several added conditions to the
  ordinance, that if the property owners want to get in on the
  tailgating, they will have to hire a host, have a food truck with
  music, if the people who come to that location for the tailgate
  exceeds 20-25 people, the property owner will have to have a
  security guard on the premises for safety sake. Make it a
  requirement for the property owners and it will keep everyone safe
  while they have a real good time at the tailgating event prior to
  the game.

Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and asked for a motion from the
Planning Commission.

MOTION:
The motion was made by Commissioner Rice to affirm categorical
exemption EA-CE-2020-040, and adopt a resolution recommending City
Council adoption of Zoning Code Amendment 2020-001 (ZCA-2020-001)
with several added conditions; 1) that all tailgating will be a
City-wide event and must have a host at each location; 2) each
location must have a food truck that will work with the host for food
and drink service, merchandising sales, and provided music; and 3)
if more than 20-25 people attending the tailgating, property owner
must have a licensed security guard for the protection of not only
the property owner, the host and for the attendees at the tailgating
event; and was seconded by Commissioner Shaw-Williams that
Resolution No. 1894;

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING AND
  RECOMMENDING TO THE CITY COUNCIL FOR APPROVAL
  ZONING CODE AMENDMENT 2020-001 (ZCA-2020-001)
  TO AMEND CHAPTER 12 OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL
  CODE (IMC) TO MODIFY REGULATIOINS FOR OFF-HOUR
  PARKING FOR MAJOR EVENT PATRONS AND TAILGATING
  CITYWIDE.

Be approved.

There are no appeal options as it is automatically forwarded to the
City Council, per Ms. Wilcox.
(6) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

None, confirmed by the AT&T Operator.
Chairman Springs closed the Public Comments and sked for

  7
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
April 14, 2021

(7) COMMISSION INITIATIVES:

Commissioner Patrick -
1. Question for Staff - Construction on the corner of Manchester
  Boulevard and Osage, former location of the Mrs. B’s M&M
  Restaurant, what will that eventually become?
  - Ms. Wilcox commented it will become a Starbucks.

Commissioner Rice stated –
1. Question to Staff – Regarding the City’s new street pavings and
  re-conditioning of the streets, but there are many people making
  donuts and wheelies all on the major thoroughfares, blocking
  traffic and destroying the newly paved streets, is there a way that
  the City can possibly increase the fines assessed to the drivers

  - Ms. Wilcox stated that staff can forward on the Commissioner’s
  comments to the police.

Commissioner Trejo stated –
1. Question to Staff - Regarding the Gas Station, that used to be
  a gas station located at the corner of Inglewood Avenue and Century
  Boulevard, which is now an auto repair station. There are cars
  parked all over the property, I believe are waiting to be repaired.
  Out of the eight gas pumps on site, only two pumps are available
  for service, due to all of the vehicles. The vehicles look
  terrible, the station area itself is not kept clear of debris. Is
  it possible for staff to look at the permits assigned to site to
  see if they have permits for this type of business?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that staff will contact Code Enforcement.
2. We have been having several conversations during our Planning
  Commission Meetings regarding parking and tailgating, and with the
  letter from the Inglewood Resident written about the residents not
  having parking their personal vehicles needing permits for their
  own vehicles, has there been any conversation about the local
  residents being able to have access to parking permits for their
  own vehicles so that they can readily park on the streets and not
  worry about being/receiving a ticket or being towed.
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that the City has adopted a parking permit
  program and is managed by Public Works.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams stated she enjoyed her 1st very
informative 2021 Planning Commissioner’s Academy Conference, and
looking forward to attending her second next year

Chairman Springs stated –
1. April is National Realtor’s Month, his particular office did a food
  drive for the local community, and he wanted to invite all to go
